ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** Both sections cover the recap, the transition to multimodality, and why text-only systems fail on visually-rich content. The generated section names financial reports, medical documents, and building sketches directly (all three of the expected section's named examples) plus technical diagrams as a complementary addition.

Limitations of Traditional Document Processing:
**1:** Both sections cover the OCR pipeline, rigid/fragile/costly framing, cascading errors, specific failure-mode statistics, and name building sketches/X-rays as complex-layout examples. All substantive ideas present in the expected section are present here.

Foundations of Multimodal LLMs:
**1:** Both sections cover both architectures, image encoders (all three: CLIP, OpenCLIP, SigLIP), embedding alignment, the model landscape, modality extension, and the diffusion distinction. This version is unusually rich with additional grounded material (robotics sensor-fusion analogy, theoretical alignment grounding, LLaVA's specific projection mechanism, video-surveillance and film/VFX applications) -- all accepted complementary additions that do not displace any expected idea.

Applying Multimodal LLMs to Images and PDFs:
**0:** Most of the walkthrough matches the expected section: raw bytes, Base64, public URLs, private-data-lake URLs (with the mocked GCS code example), object detection, and PDF-as-bytes. However, two ideas present in the expected section are absent: (1) the two-image comparison demonstration, and (2) processing PDFs as a Base64-encoded string -- the section goes from PDF-as-bytes directly to PDF-page object detection, skipping the Base64 treatment entirely.

Foundations of Multimodal RAG:
**0:** Both sections cover the generic RAG architecture, ColPali's OCR-bypassing role, the bag-of-embeddings representation, and the ViDoRe 81.3% figure. As in every replicate graded so far, the PaliGemma-3B/SigLIP model composition and the GitHub repository reference are both absent -- the same specific pair of named facts missing across all articles graded this session.

Implementing Multimodal RAG for Images, PDFs and Text:
**1:** Both sections cover the image grid, create_vector_index, the helper functions, search_multimodal, both example queries, and a closing synthesis statement about extending the unified index to other modalities (video frames, audio spectrograms) that closely mirrors the expected section's own framing. The one gap -- a missing demonstration of the vector_index's keys/first-element content -- is a single minor omission.

Building Multimodal AI Agents:
**1:** Both sections cover the ways multimodal capability is added to agents, tool-wrapping, building the ReAct agent, and the kitten-color question through to the final answer, plus a rich, well-anchored addition on ReAct tool-hallucination failure modes. As in every replicate graded so far, the expected section's Figure 23 (ReAct agent architecture image) has no counterpart, but this is a Flow matter, not a CoreContent one.

Conclusion:
**0:** Both sections frame the lesson as the close of Part 1 and recap the course arc. However, the expected section's specific claim -- that the Part 2 capstone's research agent will handle multimodal data and pass it to the writer agent -- is absent; the generated section previews Part 2 only as 'an interconnected research and writing agent system using LangGraph' with no multimodal connection stated. This is the section's one substantive miss, consistent with roughly half the articles graded this session.

References:
**1:** Both sections contain a numbered list of references serving the same bibliographic purpose.
